start_here: Say to your AI: "Say 'Three stores said yes.' out loud in the car voice." It runs tool:say-with-a-voice-model with that text and the place car, makes the sound on your own computer, keeps it in your files under /Voice/Said/ and hands back the file, the voice and the speed to play it at.

lists.label: Voices
lists.holds: One voice the person can be spoken to in: a shared voice or one made from their own recording, and how fast it talks.
alike: the voices list in a text-to-speech app
a spreadsheet of voice names and speeds

lists.label: Where Trillion speaks
lists.holds: One place Trillion talks to the person or for them, the voice it uses there and how fast.
alike: a table of where each voice is used

instructions: 1. Pour the two example voices into your own voices list (see pour), or let the first tool:voices run make list:voices and list:where-trillion-speaks for you with their starter rows.
2. Optionally run tool:voices to see which voice is chosen and tool:voices with make to add a voice from your own recording.

3. Say: "Say <your words> out loud", adding a place such as car or calls when you want that place's voice and speed. The AI runs tool:say-with-a-voice-model at @workshop-tools with {text, place?, voice?}.

4. Read the answer: file (the kept sound's identity), name (where it sits in your files), voice, engine, passed_over (voices that could not be made, and why) and speed (the pace your player applies); a place that does not exist or text over 2000 characters comes back as an error that says what to change.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than least_coverage of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
